### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. cardiomyopathy, dilated, 2l  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.698)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:15710)

**Proposed mechanism:** LDB3 (HGNC:15710) —DISRUPTS→ Z-disc assembly and sarcomere organization (GO:0031012); Z-disc assembly and sarcomere organization (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy, dilated (MONDO:0979236); Z-disc assembly and sarcomere organization (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1B (MONDO:0012277). Loss-of-function mutations in LDB3 disrupt Z-disc assembly and sarcomere organization, leading to dilated cardiomyopathy and autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1B.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in LDB3 with a gain-of-function mechanism or a dominant-negative effect would falsify this hypothesis. Alternatively, the absence of mutations in LDB3 in well-characterized patients with these distinct phenotypes would also be falsifying. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high frequency (>1%) of loss-of-function variants in LDB3 in the general population would suggest incomplete penetrance or alternative causal mechanisms.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism mediated by LDB3 could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both dilated cardiomyopathy and limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1B, potentially by stabilizing Z-disc structure or improving sarcomere function.

**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:15710)

**Proposed mechanism:** LDB3 (HGNC:15710) —DISRUPTS→ Z-disc organization and assembly (GO:0035104); Z-disc organization and assembly (GO:0035104) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy, dilated (HP:0001643); Z-disc organization and assembly (GO:0035104) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy, distal, with rimmed vacuoles (HP:0003702). Loss-of-function mutations in LDB3 disrupt its role in Z-disc organization and assembly, leading to both dilated cardiomyopathy (MONDO:0011094) and distal myopathy with rimmed vacuoles (MONDO:0012277).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in LDB3 that lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if specific molecular pathways downstream of LDB3 disruption are found to be distinct for each disease, this would suggest separate mechanisms. _(variant: rs74315373)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting LDB3 or its downstream effectors in the Z-disc could offer therapeutic strategies for both dilated cardiomyopathy and distal myopathy with rimmed vacuoles.
